rejectedRevisions.reason: The bounded runtime completed no promotable result because an HTTP/1.1 connection remained in CLOSE_WAIT/FIN_WAIT_2 and server cleanup did not finish.

confirmedFacts.sample: one HTTP/1.1 and one HTTP/2 unary request
confirmedFacts.fact: Both clients received DeadlineExceeded after the command had committed; both handlers observed abort, retry returned replay, and one command remained.

confirmedFacts.sample: one HTTP/1.1 socket drop and one HTTP/2 session drop after event 3 of 10
confirmedFacts.fact: The stream surfaced an error and did not auto-resubscribe. An explicit request using the last durable cursor returned exactly events 4 through 10.

confirmedFacts.sample: one uncheckpointed event on each protocol
confirmedFacts.fact: Reconnecting from the previous durable cursor redelivered the same stable event ID on both protocols.

confirmedFacts.sample: expired, forged, wrong-stream, and ahead cursors on both protocols
confirmedFacts.fact: All eight cases failed with the expected Connect code and a typed CursorErrorDetail reason.

confirmedFacts.sample: 128 events of 65536 bytes on each protocol
confirmedFacts.fact: While the client paused after its first event, the server generator produced all 128 events on both protocols. Cancellation arrived after production completed, so built-in transport backpressure did not impose an application memory budget for this sample.

confirmedFacts.sample: one idle HTTP/2 GOAWAY followed by a new unary command
confirmedFacts.fact: The pinned 2.1.2 client opened a usable successor session and the next command succeeded.

architectureInvariants: A unary timeout is an unknown command outcome; retry only with the same durable command ID and semantic fingerprint.
Connect does not own stream replay. SDKs explicitly reconnect with a durable opaque cursor.
Event delivery is at least once across an uncheckpointed reconnect; consumers deduplicate by stable event ID and persist the cursor only with their projection.
Bind opaque cursors cryptographically to tenant, stream, projection version, retention epoch, and sequence.
Return typed expired, forged, wrong-stream, and ahead cursor errors without silently resetting to latest.
Enforce per-subscriber queued-event and queued-byte budgets in the application layer; do not treat transport backpressure as the budget.
Bound and attest connection/session cleanup; an RPC ending does not prove every transport handle closed.
HTTP/2 GOAWAY recovery is adapter behavior, not command replay authority.
